Since these patches are applied during the prepare() function and are explicitly in scope for injection attacks, their contents must be reviewed before a safe verdict can be issued.
data.disagreement_analysis: The qwen3-235b model returned 'inconclusive' due to HTTP 400 API errors when auditing .SRCINFO and .nvchecker.toml, while deepseek-v4-flash successfully reviewed those files and returned 'safe'. The disagreement stems from tooling failures rather than analytical differences. However, both models share the same critical coverage gap: skipping the patch files.
coverage_issues: Both models incorrectly classified .patch files as binary and skipped them. Patch files are plain text and must be reviewed when applied during build.
qwen3-235b failed to audit .SRCINFO and .nvchecker.toml due to API errors (HTTP 400), leaving those files unverified.
false_negatives: Neither model reviewed 0001-cmake-Install-kde-wallpaper-to-correct-path.patch or 0002-cmake-Install-gnome-extensions-separately.patch. These patches execute during prepare() and could contain malicious commands or path traversal attacks.
learnings: File type detection must not rely solely on extension or MIME heuristics that misclassify .patch files as binary. Patch files should always be treated as text and audited when referenced in PKGBUILD functions.
API errors during file review should trigger automatic retries or escalation rather than silently marking files as inconclusive.
When multiple models skip the same files, the audit orchestrator should flag this as a shared coverage gap and commission a targeted re-audit of those specific files.
